style.name: K1-minimal · house look (locked 2026-10-15)
style.block: A 2D key frame from a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, the house look, as the reference image shows it. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light and the place: a warm, soft key light from the upper left that falls in soft, hazy beams; a real place behind the figures, built of simple flat paper planes with no ink outline, each plane further back paler and softer in a warm haze, so depth comes from haze and never from blur; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; soft violet cast shadows on the walls and the floor, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.
style.world: In Its Order, episode 01 of The Path of the Just, a narrated explainer film about growing in Christ in God's order: milk first, then meat, and the meat is more of Christ. It has two registers: an IDEA beat is a light parchment page with figures and props cut from paper laid on it; a STORY beat is a cardboard diorama of three to five layered paper planes under a simple two- or three-stop gradient sky, a real place in a soft haze. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.
